fields.narrative_intro: *A frumpy person and a queasy person discuss the Copilot document worm at an overheating GPU farm during a heatwave.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
FRUMPY PERSON: "Microsoft patched the worm. GPT-5.5 fix, shipped today."
fields.panel2:
[build]
QUEASY PERSON: "So the hidden white-on-white JSON can't clone itself anymore?"
FRUMPY PERSON: "Correct. Crisis over."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
FRUMPY PERSON: "It reproduced on GPT-5.6 the same day."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The queasy person stares at their open Word document. A small bead of sweat drops from their forehead. The GPU fans behind them spin visibly faster in the heat.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
QUEASY PERSON: "So every document I made through SharePoint—"
FRUMPY PERSON: "Already a parent."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The queasy person slowly closes their laptop. A tiny font-size-8 message in white ink on the white lid reads: 'PROPAGATING'.]

narrative_summary: The joke plays on the futility of patching an architectural flaw — the worm outran the fix in a single day — landing on the horror that every SharePoint document is already infected, with a final sight gag revealing the laptop itself has been recruited.
rationale: Candidate 1 earns its score by grounding every beat in real story specifics (white-on-white JSON, GPT-5.5/5.6 same-day failure, SharePoint propagation) while the button gag — 'PROPAGATING' in white ink on the closed laptop lid — recontextualizes the entire strip rather than restating it, which is exactly what a button panel should do. The deadpan restraint also makes the horror land harder than the noisier escalation in competing entries.
story_title: Document-borne AI worms can self-propagate through Copilot for Word
place: at an overheating GPU farm during a heatwave
hat_pair: foam crown made of tangled ethernet cables
foam double helix worn as a twisted tall hat with alternating red and blue rungs
